question: Türkiye is doing everything it can to legitimise the illegal, such as the pseudo-state’s participation in the Organisation of Turkic States. Together with Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Hungary, it has accepted the so-called “Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus” as an observer, thus indirectly recognising this political construct as a state entity.

In other words, there has been an attempt to place the pseudo-state on an equal footing with any recognised state. At the very last moment, through the efforts of the Republic of Cyprus, the pseudo-state was blocked from participating. I should point out that the EU is Kazakhstan’s first trading partner and first foreign investor.
Kazakhstan remains the EU’s main trading partner in Central Asia, with the balance of trade in its favour. In view of this: 1.
What actions will the Commission take to counter the efforts of states such as Kazakhstan to achieve recognition for the Cypriot occupied territories?
Will the same actions apply to the various international forums and sessions of organisations such as the Organisation of Turkic States?
answer: The EU has monitored with concern developments since the Organisation of Turkic States (OTS) summit in Samarkand (Uzbekistan), in November 2022, regarding the acceptance of the so-called, internationally not recognised, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) as an observer to this organisation. A statement of the Spokesperson was issued, expressing a clear position against these developments (1).

The EU has actively and continuously expressed these preoccupations to the members of the OTS, at all levels. The EU took note that no representative of the so-called TRNC participated in the tenth summit of the OTS, which was held in Astana (Kazakhstan) on 3 November 2023.

The EU continues to call upon Kazakhstan and other members of the OTS not to implement any decision which would allow for the so-called, internationally not recognised, TRNC to acquire observer status in the OTS. Such actions undermine efforts to relaunch the Cyprus settlement talks.

The EU remains completely committed to ensuring that the relevant United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolution s (2) and generally recognised principles and norms of international law, particularly with respect to the sovereignty, independence and integrity of states, are fully upheld.
